correctness.rationale: Exact 14-vertex Fano-incidence model and 42-angle exact-cover recurrence enumerate every admissible seven-hexagon face system. All eight pass coherent opposite-edge orientation constraints, Euler characteristic zero, and \(K_7\) dual check. Exhaustive enumeration of 24 matching permutations and every face-alternating six-cycle constructs the 21 switching edges per embedding and checks 3 disjoint \(C_7\) plus 3 isolated, each face occurring once on each \(C_7\). A second independent cyclic-difference-set/bitmask implementation confirms all eight systems, factorization triples, and 2-fold incidences. Both verifiers are self-contained and fully replay from supplied files. The parity of face boundaries in a connected face-dual proves any odd flip cycle has at least seven moves. No general/infinite conclusion is claimed.

value.rationale: The seven-face Heawood map is the canonical minimum symmetric toroidal polyhex. The result resolves its natural full-face resonance state space exactly, identifies the smallest possible odd flip loops from the dual \(K_7\) mod-2 incidence, and explains three frozen configurations through an embedding-to-one-factorization bijection. This gives a natural sharp boundary for the published proper-face-subset hypercube/bipartiteness theorem and is not an arbitrary numerical slice. For any proper face subset the same result yields a forest with exactly \(24-3|\mathscr S|\) connected components, so non-bipartiteness appears sharply when the last face is admitted.
